auditMetadata.productionReadinessVerdict: GO (All 14 audit findings BACKEND-001..BACKEND-014 FIXED AND VERIFIED; typecheck exit 0; 68/68 tests passing across 16 suites with 0 failed, 0 skipped, and 0 orphan DB records; ensure deployment secrets CRON_SECRET and STORAGE_WEBHOOK_SECRET are populated in runtime env)

documentationDriftNotes: apps/api/docs/endpoints.md:275 still lists accessToken in POST /api/v1/auth/login JSON example, whereas BACKEND-002 keeps both accessToken and refreshToken in HttpOnly cookies only.
operationalConfigurationRisks: CRON_SECRET and STORAGE_WEBHOOK_SECRET are unset in local apps/api/.env and apps/web/.env* (endpoints intentionally fail closed with 401 until configured in deployment env).
Root .env still contains short legacy JWT_SECRET (20 chars) and JWT_REFRESH_SECRET (24 chars), unused when running apps/api directly from apps/api/.env (64-char secrets).
Local apps/api/.env sets NODE_ENV=production, enabling trust proxy = 1 and secure cookie flags.

findings.title: Spoofable IP rate limiting, pre-auth cron DoS ordering, unref-less interval leak, and missing route rate limiters

steps: Send 3 unauthenticated GET /api/v1/cron/news-crawl requests sharing x-forwarded-for: 198.51.100.201 (no x-cron-secret).
Send a 4th GET /api/v1/cron/news-crawl from the same IP WITH valid x-cron-secret.

findings.expectedBehavior: cronNewsCrawlRateLimiter must only count/run after verifyCronSecret succeeds so unauthenticated traffic cannot lock out the real cron scheduler, clientIp must not trust raw spoofable X-Forwarded-For without Express trust proxy validation, cleanup interval must call .unref(), and mutating routes (/auth/device, /auth/refresh, /reports/:id/vote, /reports/:id/updates, /users/verify, /routes/safe-path) must enforce bounded rate limits.
findings.actualBehavior: On the 4th (authenticated) call in regression testing, the endpoint returned HTTP 429 RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED instead of 200 (429 !== 200). clientIp reads req.headers['x-forwarded-for'] directly, allowing trivial IP spoofing to bypass authLoginRateLimiter, while setInterval lacks .unref().
findings.rootCause: Middleware chain in apps/api/src/routes/cron.ts:36-37 registers cronNewsCrawlRateLimiter before verifyCronSecret, and rateLimiter.ts:34-37 splits req.headers['x-forwarded-for'] regardless of proxy trust.
findings.recommendedFix: 1) Reorder cron.ts middleware so verifyCronSecret runs before cronNewsCrawlRateLimiter. 2) Use req.ip with explicit Express trust proxy configuration instead of trusting raw X-Forwarded-For strings. 3) Call .unref() on cleanup interval timers in rateLimiter.ts:10-18. 4) Add calibrated rate limiters to /auth/device, /auth/refresh, /reports/:id/vote, /reports/:id/updates, /users/verify, and /routes/safe-path.
findings.regressionTestName: [BACKEND-001] Unauthenticated calls to /api/v1/cron/news-crawl must NOT exhaust authenticated cron rate-limit quota on same IP
acceptanceCriteria: 3+ unauthenticated requests to /api/v1/cron/news-crawl return 401 and never consume legitimate cron quota for that IP.
Subsequent authenticated request with valid secret returns 200.
Spoofed X-Forwarded-For headers do not reset per-client login quota when direct socket connection originates from the same peer.

postFixVerification.implementedFixSummary: Reordered cron.ts so verifyCronSecret runs before cronNewsCrawlRateLimiter; added .unref() on rateLimiter cleanup timer; switched clientIp to Express req.ip with trust proxy setting in app.ts; calibrated rate limiters on /auth/device, /auth/refresh, /reports/:id/vote, /reports/:id/updates, /users/verify, and /routes/safe-path.
postFixVerification.actualResultAfterFix: Unauthenticated /cron/news-crawl GET & POST return 401 without exhausting authenticated cron quota (subsequent authenticated request returns 200); .unref() confirmed on cleanup interval; newly added limiters enforce 429 cleanly; spoofed X-Forwarded-For does not bypass /auth/login limiter.

findings.title: Token exposure in /auth/login JSON, lack of refreshToken rotation, and broken expired-access /auth/logout

steps: Replay the exact same old refreshToken on a second POST /api/v1/auth/refresh.

findings.expectedBehavior: /auth/login should rely strictly on HttpOnly cookies (omitting raw refreshToken from JSON body), /auth/refresh must rotate and revoke the prior refreshToken on each use (returning 401 on replay), and /auth/logout must clear cookies and revoke any presented refreshToken cookie even if the short-lived accessToken has already expired.
findings.actualBehavior: POST /api/v1/auth/login includes accessToken and refreshToken in JSON data; replaying an already-used refreshToken on POST /api/v1/auth/refresh returned HTTP 200 instead of 401 (200 !== 401); POST /api/v1/auth/logout rejects callers with an expired accessToken via requireAuth (401) before revoking RefreshToken.
findings.rootCause: authController.ts serializes token strings into JSON data; authService.ts:83-98 validates RefreshToken without revoking/re-issuing a new token row; routes/auth.ts:27 gates /logout behind requireAuth.
findings.recommendedFix: 1) Stop returning refreshToken (and accessToken where HttpOnly cookies suffice) in login JSON body unless required by an explicit non-cookie client contract. 2) Implement single-use refresh token rotation in authService: revoke old RefreshToken row inside a transaction, issue a new refreshToken + cookie, and revoke user family tokens if replay is detected. 3) Remove strict requireAuth gate on /auth/logout or decode/validate the refreshToken cookie directly so expired access tokens still allow clean server-side revocation and cookie clearing.
findings.regressionTestName: [BACKEND-002] /auth/login should not leak refreshToken in JSON, /auth/refresh must rotate refreshToken, and /auth/logout must work with expired accessToken
acceptanceCriteria: POST /api/v1/auth/login response JSON omits refreshToken.
Replaying a previously consumed refreshToken returns 401.
POST /api/v1/auth/logout with an expired accessToken and valid refreshToken returns 200, revokes DB RefreshToken, and clears auth cookies.

postFixVerification.implementedFixSummary: Omitted accessToken and refreshToken from /auth/login JSON response (HttpOnly cookies only, preserving socketToken); implemented transactional single-use refreshToken rotation + replay rejection (401) in /auth/refresh; added signature-verified expired-access handling in /auth/logout so DB RefreshToken revocation and cookie clearing succeed with 200.
postFixVerification.actualResultAfterFix: Login JSON omits accessToken and refreshToken; /auth/refresh rotates DB RefreshToken and HttpOnly cookies and rejects replayed tokens with 401; /auth/logout with an expired accessToken + valid refreshToken cookie returns 200, marks DB RefreshToken revoked, and clears auth cookies. (Note: apps/api/docs/endpoints.md:275 still mentions accessToken in JSON example.)

findings.title: Hardcoded fallback JWT secrets in env.ts and short (<32-char) JWT secrets in runtime .env
findings.expectedBehavior: Startup configuration must fail closed when JWT_SECRET or JWT_REFRESH_SECRET are absent or below 32 characters (256-bit HS256 minimum entropy), with zero hardcoded default fallback strings.
findings.actualBehavior: env.ts:12-13 defines hardcoded fallbacks ('super-secret-access-key-replace-in-prod' and 'super-secret-refresh-key-replace-in-prod'), and current apps/api/.env configures JWT_SECRET length 20 (<32) and JWT_REFRESH_SECRET length 24 (<32).
findings.rootCause: Permissive string fallbacks in env.ts:12-13 instead of startup Zod schema validation enforcing non-empty >=32-character secrets.
findings.recommendedFix: Remove hardcoded JWT secret fallbacks from env.ts:12-13, validate JWT_SECRET and JWT_REFRESH_SECRET at boot with z.string().min(32), and rotate .env secrets to >=32 random characters.
findings.regressionTestName: [BACKEND-003] JWT_SECRET and JWT_REFRESH_SECRET in .env must be >= 32 characters without hardcoded fallbacks
acceptanceCriteria: JWT_SECRET and JWT_REFRESH_SECRET in .env are >= 32 characters.
Boot fails cleanly if either secret is missing or under 32 characters, with no default strings in env.ts.

postFixVerification.implementedFixSummary: Removed hardcoded fallback JWT secret strings in env.ts and enforced >= 32 characters via Zod at boot; rotated JWT_SECRET and JWT_REFRESH_SECRET in apps/api/.env to 64 characters.
postFixVerification.actualResultAfterFix: apps/api/.env secrets pass >= 32-character check and booting env.ts with missing or short (<32-char) JWT_SECRET / JWT_REFRESH_SECRET fails closed immediately.

findings.title: POST /api/v1/reports accepts empty "" and unbounded description strings
findings.expectedBehavior: Optional description must be trimmed and bounded (e.g., 1..1000 chars when provided) so empty/whitespace strings and oversized payloads fail with 400 Bad Request.
findings.actualBehavior: POST /api/v1/reports returned 201 Created for description: "" (assertion 201 !== 400) and accepts arbitrarily long strings (>1500 chars).
findings.rootCause: reportSchema defines description: z.string().optional() without .trim(), .min(1), or .max(1000).
findings.recommendedFix: Update apps/api/src/routes/reports.ts:34 to validate description: z.string().trim().min(1).max(1000).optional() (or explicit null/undefined handling when omitted).
findings.regressionTestName: [BACKEND-004] POST /api/v1/reports must reject empty string "" and >1000-char description with 400
acceptanceCriteria: POST /api/v1/reports with description: "" or whitespace returns 400.
POST /api/v1/reports with description > 1000 characters returns 400.
Omitted description (undefined) still succeeds with 201.

postFixVerification.actualResultAfterFix: Empty "", whitespace-only, and 1001-char descriptions return 400; 1000-char valid descriptions and omitted descriptions return 201.

findings.title: POST /api/v1/reports/:id/updates persists whitespace-only update strings as empty content
findings.expectedBehavior: Whitespace-only content ("   ") must fail Zod validation with 400 Bad Request because trimmed length is 0 (< min 2).
findings.actualBehavior: Schema check runs before trimming, passes 3 spaces (>= min 2), and service trims to "" — returning HTTP 201 Created instead of 400 (201 !== 400).
findings.rootCause: addUpdateSchema at reports.ts:82 uses z.string().min(2).max(500) without .trim().
findings.regressionTestName: [BACKEND-005] POST /api/v1/reports/:id/updates must reject whitespace-only content with 400
acceptanceCriteria: POST /api/v1/reports/:id/updates with content: "   " returns 400 Bad Request and inserts no row.

postFixVerification.implementedFixSummary: Added .trim() before .min(2).max(500) on addUpdateSchema.body.content in apps/api/src/routes/reports.ts.
postFixVerification.actualResultAfterFix: Whitespace-only "   " and " a " fail with 400; valid trimmed content >= 2 chars returns 201.

findings.title: GET /api/v1/safe-zones accepts non-numeric spatial query params (?lat=abc&lng=def) and returns 200 []
findings.expectedBehavior: Non-numeric spatial query coordinates must be rejected with 400 Bad Request.
findings.actualBehavior: Endpoint returned HTTP 200 OK with empty array [] instead of 400 (200 !== 400).
findings.rootCause: safeZoneQuerySchema accepts optional strings without numeric/finite-number refinement, causing parseFloat("abc") -> NaN downstream.
findings.recommendedFix: Validate numeric format and geographic range (-90..90 lat, -180..180 lng, positive radius) in safeZoneQuerySchema.
findings.regressionTestName: [BACKEND-006] GET /api/v1/safe-zones must return 400 for non-numeric spatial parameters (?lat=abc&lng=def)
acceptanceCriteria: GET /api/v1/safe-zones?lat=abc&lng=def returns 400 Bad Request.
Out-of-range lat/lng values or non-numeric radius/bounds return 400.

postFixVerification.implementedFixSummary: Enforced strict numeric regex, finite latitude (-90..90), longitude (-180..180), positive radius, and complete/ordered bounding box validation in apps/api/src/routes/safeZones.ts and safeZoneController.ts.
postFixVerification.actualResultAfterFix: Non-numeric params, trailing garbage (90.3abc), out-of-range coordinates (lat=95), negative radius, partial params, and inverted bounds return 400 Bad Request.

findings.title: Missing resource UUIDs return 400 Bad Request instead of 404 Not Found across three endpoints
findings.module: Votes, Alert Zones & User Verification Controllers
findings.expectedBehavior: Valid UUID referencing a non-existent Report, UserAlertZone, or UserVerification must return HTTP 404 Not Found.
findings.actualBehavior: POST /api/v1/reports/<missing-uuid>/vote returned 400 instead of 404 (400 !== 404); DELETE /api/v1/alerts/zones/<missing-uuid> and POST /api/v1/users/verify/<missing-uuid>/approve also return 400.
findings.rootCause: voteService.ts and alertZoneService.ts throw bare Error without .statusCode = 404, while userController.ts:36-38 ignores error.statusCode and passes hardcoded 400.
findings.recommendedFix: Attach statusCode = 404 on not-found errors in voteService.ts and alertZoneService.ts, and preserve error.statusCode || 400 in alertController.ts, voteController.ts, and userController.ts.
findings.regressionTestName: [BACKEND-007] Missing resource IDs on /reports/:id/vote, /alerts/zones/:id, and /users/verify/:id/approve must return 404 (not 400)
acceptanceCriteria: All three endpoints return HTTP 404 Not Found when supplied a valid but non-existent UUID.

postFixVerification.implementedFixSummary: Attached statusCode = 404 to missing-target errors in voteService.ts and alertZoneService.ts and propagated error.statusCode in userController.ts.
postFixVerification.actualResultAfterFix: Non-existent valid UUIDs return HTTP 404 across POST /reports/:id/vote, DELETE /alerts/zones/:id, and POST /users/verify/:id/approve.

findings.title: POST /api/v1/auth/device returns 201 Created unconditionally on existing device re-login
findings.expectedBehavior: First device registration returns 201 Created; subsequent sign-ins for an already existing anonymousId return 200 OK.
findings.actualBehavior: Second sign-in for the same anonymousId returned 201 Created instead of 200 (201 !== 200).
findings.rootCause: authController.ts:16 hardcodes status 201 without distinguishing newly created users from existing logins returned by authService.
findings.recommendedFix: Have authService return { ..., isNewUser: boolean } so authController sends 201 only when created and 200 on repeat sign-in (and align minimum anonymousId length policy intentionally).
findings.regressionTestName: [BACKEND-008] Repeat sign-in on POST /api/v1/auth/device for existing anonymousId should return 200 OK instead of 201 Created
acceptanceCriteria: First POST /api/v1/auth/device returns 201.
Second POST /api/v1/auth/device for the same anonymousId returns 200.

postFixVerification.implementedFixSummary: Returned isNewUser from authService device login and returned 201 Created only on new anonymous user creation vs 200 OK on repeat sign-in in authController.ts.
postFixVerification.actualResultAfterFix: Initial POST /api/v1/auth/device returns 201 Created; repeat sign-in with the same anonymousId returns 200 OK.

findings.title: API contract & type inconsistencies (string distanceMeters, clamped /admin/logs, raw JSON / & /media/webhook)
findings.module: Safe Zones, Admin, Media Webhook, Root & Health Routes
findings.expectedBehavior: Radial /safe-zones returns numeric distanceMeters ('number'), /admin/logs rejects invalid/out-of-range limit>100 with 400 instead of silent clamping, and JSON responses consistently use the { success, data } envelope.
findings.actualBehavior: Radial GET /api/v1/safe-zones returned typeof distanceMeters === 'string' ('string' !== 'number'); GET /api/v1/admin/logs?limit=101 silently clamps rather than returning 400; POST /api/v1/media/webhook returns { received: true } without { success, data }.
findings.rootCause: Postgres numeric type from ROUND(...::numeric, 1) serializes as string in Node/Prisma; adminService clamps limit silently; mediaController and health/root handlers emit ad-hoc JSON objects.
findings.recommendedFix: Cast distanceMeters to FLOAT/Number in safeZoneService.ts:207, validate /admin/logs page/limit bounds with Zod, and standardize success envelopes across endpoints (coordinating any breaking frontend/cron consumer updates).
findings.regressionTestName: [BACKEND-009] API contract consistency: /media/webhook uses {success,data}, /admin/logs rejects limit>100, and /safe-zones distanceMeters is a number
acceptanceCriteria: typeof zone.distanceMeters === 'number'.
GET /api/v1/admin/logs?limit=101 returns 400.
POST /api/v1/media/webhook returns { success: true, data: ... }.

postFixVerification.implementedFixSummary: Cast distanceMeters to number in safeZoneService.ts; replaced silent clamping with strict Zod query validation on /admin/logs and /admin/analytics/trends; standardized /, /health, /health/db, /api/v1/health, /api/v1/health/db, and /media/webhook to { success, data } envelopes.
postFixVerification.actualResultAfterFix: typeof distanceMeters === "number"; /admin/logs rejects limit>100, non-numeric limit, page<1, and extra params with 400; /admin/analytics/trends rejects invalid query params with 400; /, /health*, and /media/webhook return { success: true, data }.

findings.title: Admin KYC rejection writes identical ModerationLog.action ('VERIFY_USER') + duplicate /users/verify/:id/approve route
findings.expectedBehavior: Rejecting KYC must record a distinct ModerationAction enum value (e.g., REJECT_VERIFICATION) rather than sharing VERIFY_USER with approvals, and verification approval should use one canonical validated route.
findings.actualBehavior: Rejected KYC inserts ModerationLog row with action === 'VERIFY_USER' identically to approvals, and both /users/verify/:id/approve and /admin/verifications/:id/approve coexist with mismatched shapes.
findings.rootCause: ModerationAction enum lacked a rejection variant when rejectVerification was added, reusing VERIFY_USER with a reason prefix; legacy /users/verify/:id/approve was left mounted.
findings.recommendedFix: Add REJECT_VERIFICATION (or distinct ModerationAction) via additive Prisma migration in rejectVerification, and deprecate/align /users/verify/:id/approve with UUID validation.
findings.regressionTestName: [BACKEND-010] Admin verification rejection must record a distinct rejection ModerationLog.action instead of VERIFY_USER
acceptanceCriteria: ModerationLog created by rejectVerification uses a distinct rejection action rather than VERIFY_USER.
Approval endpoint behavior and UUID validation are consistent.

postFixVerification.implementedFixSummary: Added ModerationAction.REJECT_VERIFICATION in schema.prisma, updated rejectVerification in userService.ts and log filter validation in adminService.ts/admin routes, and enforced verifyIdParamSchema UUID validation on legacy /users/verify/:id/approve.
postFixVerification.actualResultAfterFix: Verification rejection logs REJECT_VERIFICATION, GET /admin/logs?action=REJECT_VERIFICATION returns filtered rows cleanly, and invalid UUID on /users/verify/:id/approve returns 400.

findings.title: POST /api/v1/reports and POST /api/v1/reports/:id/vote expose reporter userId PII in JSON responses
findings.expectedBehavior: Report creation and voting responses must strip userId (matching sanitizeReportOutput in GET /reports and GET /reports/:id) so anonymous reporters cannot be correlated by other authenticated users.
findings.actualBehavior: Both POST /api/v1/reports and POST /api/v1/reports/:id/vote return raw Prisma Report records containing userId ('userId' in response === true, breaking assertion true !== false). Any authenticated voter can harvest another reporter's account UUID.
findings.rootCause: reportService.ts:182-187 spreads the raw Prisma report record and voteService.ts:105 returns raw result from prisma.report.update without passing through PII sanitization.
findings.recommendedFix: Run return payloads of createReport and castVote through sanitizeReportOutput / explicit DTO projection omitting userId (attaching only isOwner/fuzzed coords where appropriate).
findings.regressionTestName: [BACKEND-011] POST /api/v1/reports and POST /api/v1/reports/:id/vote must NOT expose reporter userId PII in response JSON
acceptanceCriteria: 'userId' property is absent from POST /api/v1/reports response data.
'userId' property is absent from POST /api/v1/reports/:id/vote response data.

postFixVerification.implementedFixSummary: Passed createReport and castVote responses through sanitizeReportOutput to strip reporter userId PII while preserving ownership/coordinate logic.
postFixVerification.actualResultAfterFix: Both POST /api/v1/reports and POST /api/v1/reports/:id/vote exclude reporter userId from response JSON.

findings.title: GET /api/v1/reports accepts inverted bounding boxes (minLng > maxLng / minLat > maxLat) with 200 OK
findings.expectedBehavior: Inverted or invalid viewport bounds (minLng >= maxLng or minLat >= maxLat) and malformed numeric prefixes like '90.3abc' must be rejected with 400 Bad Request.
findings.actualBehavior: GET /api/v1/reports with minLng=90.5 and maxLng=90.3 returned 200 OK instead of 400 (200 !== 400).
findings.rootCause: boundsSchema at reports.ts:53-63 only checks !isNaN(parseFloat(val)) per individual field with no numeric range check, regex strictness, or .refine(minLng < maxLng && minLat < maxLat).
findings.recommendedFix: Validate strict finite numbers in geographic range and enforce minLng < maxLng and minLat < maxLat via Zod .superRefine/.refine in boundsSchema.
findings.regressionTestName: [BACKEND-012] GET /api/v1/reports must reject inverted bounds (minLng >= maxLng or minLat >= maxLat) with 400
acceptanceCriteria: GET /api/v1/reports with minLng >= maxLng or minLat >= maxLat returns 400 Bad Request.

postFixVerification.implementedFixSummary: Added strict coordQueryParam numeric format, geographic range validation (-90..90 lat, -180..180 lng), and minLng < maxLng / minLat < maxLat bounds refinement to GET /api/v1/reports.
postFixVerification.actualResultAfterFix: Inverted bounds (minLng >= maxLng or minLat >= maxLat), trailing garbage (90.3abc), and out-of-range coordinates return 400 Bad Request.

findings.title: POST /api/v1/admin/users/:id/ban allows banning peer ADMINs and self-banning

body.reason: Regression check: peer admin ban safeguard

findings.expectedBehavior: Banning another ADMIN account or the caller's own account must be rejected with 403 Forbidden to prevent privilege sabotage and accidental admin lockout.
findings.actualBehavior: Admin 1 successfully banned Admin 2 (HTTP 200 OK instead of 403, revoking Admin 2's refresh tokens) and can ban themselves (200 !== 403).
findings.rootCause: banUser in adminService.ts:28-73 only checks !targetUser (404) and targetUser.isBanned (400), lacking role === 'ADMIN' and targetUser.id === adminId guards.
findings.recommendedFix: In adminService.ts banUser, reject with statusCode = 403 when targetUser.id === adminId or targetUser.role === 'ADMIN'.
findings.regressionTestName: [BACKEND-013] POST /api/v1/admin/users/:id/ban must forbid self-banning and peer-ADMIN suspension (403)
acceptanceCriteria: POST /api/v1/admin/users/:id/ban returns 403 when target is self or another ADMIN.
Non-admin USER/VERIFIED_RESPONDER targets remain bannable (200).

postFixVerification.implementedFixSummary: Added 403 Forbidden guards in banUser (adminService.ts) when targetUser.id === adminId or targetUser.role === "ADMIN".
postFixVerification.actualResultAfterFix: Self-banning and peer-ADMIN banning both return 403 Forbidden; non-admin user suspension remains 200 OK.

findings.title: POST /api/v1/alerts/zones persists topologically invalid self-intersecting bowtie polygons
findings.expectedBehavior: Topologically invalid self-intersecting polygons must be rejected with 400 Bad Request via PostGIS ST_IsValid before insertion.
findings.actualBehavior: POST /api/v1/alerts/zones returned 201 Created and persisted the self-intersecting polygon into PostGIS (201 !== 400).
findings.rootCause: createAlertZone in alertZoneService.ts:49-100 verifies ring closure, zone count limit, and ST_Area <= 25 km², but omits ST_IsValid(ST_GeomFromText(..., 4326)).
findings.recommendedFix: Query ST_IsValid(ST_GeomFromText(wkt, 4326)) (and ST_IsSimple if needed) inside createAlertZone before inserting, throwing a 400 error if invalid.
findings.regressionTestName: [BACKEND-014] POST /api/v1/alerts/zones must reject topologically invalid self-intersecting polygons (ST_IsValid) with 400
acceptanceCriteria: Self-intersecting bowtie polygons fail with 400 Bad Request and are not persisted in UserAlertZone.
Valid convex/concave non-self-intersecting closed polygons within 25 km² continue to succeed with 201.

postFixVerification.implementedFixSummary: Added PostGIS ST_IsValid / ST_IsValidReason topology check in createAlertZone before inserting UserAlertZone.
postFixVerification.actualResultAfterFix: Self-intersecting bowtie polygons fail with 400 Bad Request and are rejected before insertion.
